name: Verdigris Arbor

detectability.signature: Gentle piezoelectric murmurs and soft green light scatter, almost like wind through leaves

proximity: Light scatters into slow green veils, lending the grove a submerged aquarium calm
Comms carry a faint crystalline chiming
contact: Settling dust orders itself into new crystalline branchlets on any surface left still
Hull plating acquires a harmless glass-green patina of accretion
prolonged_exposure: Parked vessels require de-fouling as crystal accretion thickens on exposed surfaces
Delicate sensor apertures can cloud over if left unshuttered for weeks

phenomena: Crystalline growth on exposed surfaces at a glacial pace
Prismatic refraction veils through the emerald columns
Matter spontaneously changing state as debris orders into lattice
hazards: Hull fouling by slow crystal accretion on long-parked vessels
opportunities: Rare element concentration within the column facets
Unique material synthesis from cultivated crystal shards
Chance to study rare phenomena in a perfectly safe setting
known_incidents: The miners who discovered the grove went bankrupt protecting it instead of exploiting it, and their claim charter became the template for a hundred natural monument laws
description: A grove of emerald crystal columns rises from a mineral-rich asteroid shoal, some taller than orbital elevators. Light entering the grove scatters into slow green veils that give the whole structure a submerged, aquarium calm. Passive scans return gentle piezoelectric murmurs, almost like wind through leaves.

The Arbor is motionless, growing perhaps a centimeter per decade as trace metals condense onto its facets. Dust and debris that settle on the columns slowly order themselves into new crystalline branchlets. Nothing within four thousand kilometers has ever been recorded as harmed.

Miners found the formation six centuries ago while staking claims on the shoal and promptly went bankrupt protecting it instead of exploiting it. Their claim charter became the template for a hundred natural monument laws. Crystal samples cultivated from fallen shards anchor an entire industry in precision optics.

The grove accepts visitors freely, and quiet tourism has replaced the mining trade. Researchers still cannot explain why the columns grow toward, and only toward, the galactic core. Picnickers are asked not to touch the glass-green branches.
